content: This paper presents a novel methodology for simultaneously performing feature selection and classification on longitudinal/functional data with categorical outcomes, formulating an optimization problem that combines logistic loss with functional features and solving it via functional principal components and an adaptive Dual Augmented Lagrangian algorithm designed to exploit sparsity for dimensionality reduction. The method is computationally efficient enough to handle high-dimensional settings where features greatly outnumber observations, and its effectiveness is validated through simulations and a real-world application examining the relationships between four chronic diseases and various health and socio-demographic factors.
